_comment: What the app can actually do in a SHIPPING build, versus what merely exists in the tree.
Companion to SHIPPED_VERSION.json, and it exists for the same reason. That file was
written after gunzino.me advertised a version nobody could install. On 2026-08-26 the same
failure was found in the other axis: nineteen places across three websites and the App
Store listing described Private Cloud Compute as a live capability. It has never been in
an App Store build. One of them, Fascinaiting's v4.6 release notes, stated outright that
Nothing caught it, because a version number has a marker and a capability did not.
HOW TO USE THIS. Before writing a capability into public copy -- App Store description,
What's New, any of the three websites, the README, or Settings -- check it here. A
capability with status 'built_not_enabled' must be described in the future tense.
scripts/verify_capabilities.py checks that the code behind every declared capability still
exists. It cannot prove a capability works; it proves the implementation has not been
deleted or renamed while the public claim stayed up. That is the drift that actually
happened here: Settings advertised eight agentic tools when four were wired up.
When a capability's status changes, update it here FIRST, then the copy.

on_device_retrieval.public_claim: Reading, indexing, retrieval, ranking and verification all run on your device.

on_device_generation.public_claim: Answers are written by the Apple Intelligence models already built into the device.

abstention.public_claim: When your files don't support an answer, it says so and stops.

answer_verification.public_claim: It checks the finished answer against the passages it actually used.

vision_ocr.public_claim: Images and scans, read with Vision OCR.

media_transcription.public_claim: Audio and video, transcribed on device.

quality_modes.public_claim: Choose Standard, Deep Think, or Maximum.

per_library_sync.public_claim: Choose Local Only or iCloud Drive for each library.

shortcuts_intents.public_claim: Siri and Shortcuts actions for common document and library workflows.
shortcuts_intents.note: Counted, not estimated. Settings once advertised eight agentic tools when four were wired up; that is what a count guards against.

private_cloud_compute.public_claim: Optional Apple Private Cloud Compute support is live on iOS and macOS 27. Retrieval, indexing and ranking stay on device; only the final answer may reach Apple's servers, after you consent.
private_cloud_compute.note: Flipped to 'shipping' on 2026-09-10, when iOS 5.2 and macOS 5.2 both reached READY_FOR_SALE with build 451, read from the App Store Connect API. Public copy may now use the present tense. Every path still sits behind #if compiler(>=6.4): Xcode 26.6 (Swift 6.3.3) compiles them out, Xcode 27 (Swift 6.4) in, so a build made with an older toolchain would silently lose this capability while the claim stayed true-looking. ci_scripts/ci_post_xcodebuild.sh is the guard: from 5.2 it fails on zero PrivateCloudCompute symbols against a live SystemLanguageModel control. At runtime the capability is additionally gated on iOS/macOS 27 and on the entitlement and quota check in FoundationModelRoutePolicy.isPCCAvailable, so a 26 device running this binary stays fully on-device and the in-app copy says so.

verified_by: App Store Connect API, 2026-09-10: iOS 5.2 and macOS 5.2 both READY_FOR_SALE, build 451.
